clue.text: Needed to retaliate if your opponent gets the first blow?

definitions.text: Needed to retaliate if your opponent gets the first blow?

parts.words: Needed to retaliate if your opponent gets the first blow?
parts.note: a fighter winded by an opening punch needs fresh breath before hitting back; 'blow' plays on breath as well as a punch

explanation.surface: A boxer floored by an opening punch needs something before striking back.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewed burst of energy after exhaustion is the idiom; here it is literally a recovery of breath after being winded.

clue.text: Learning Heather goes out to work for a living

indicators.note: goes out means the heather leaves the word learning

parts.note: the remaining letters do sit in the middle of this word, but by deletion of the heather word around them, not as a hidden-word device: a coincidence of the deletion
ling is a name for heather

explanation.surface: A student named Heather leaves school to take a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing L and ING from LEARNING leaves the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain money by labour is to be paid wages, a synonym.

clue.text: Love duets translated and put out

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Love songs are rendered into a new language and released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges DUETS into USTED after O.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel or eject someone is to remove them, a synonym.

parts.note: windows set high in a sloping roof, lights in the sense of windows

explanation.surface: A phrase about the standout features of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright windows projecting from a sloping roof are windows placed up high.

definitions.meaning: the military medal of Germany named for a metal

explanation.definitionFit: Both smooth creases from fabric with a hot appliance, and the Iron Cross, a German military medal.

clue.text: Sand put out for the rubbish collector

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sand is left out for the bin men to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SANDPUT; the sand put out for the bin lorry is a misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-handled pan receives sweepings, a gatherer of dirt.

indicators.note: new means the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A delegate says they stand for a fresh scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges IREPRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold undertaking or project is a scheme, so a plan.

clue.text: Having a diploma might give one a nice title

definitions.note: describes a holder of a licence or diploma; the answer is the noun for such a person

indicators.note: might give suggests the words can be reshaped into something else

explanation.surface: A qualification might earn someone a pleasant honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might give' rearranges ANICETITLE; 'one' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a licence from a college or university is a qualified graduate.

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turns tells us the word it is read backwards here

explanation.surface: Something swivels round to face an adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses IT to TI, and 'on' places that after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone against a cause is a hostile party, an adversary of it.

parts.note: the underground parts of pasture plants that cows graze, and also ordinary voters, the base members of a constituency

explanation.surface: A description of what pasture plants are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary rank-and-file members of a party are its base, while literally the plant roots are part of fodder.

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of hit may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A thug might steal from and strike a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HIT into THI, then EVE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob is to steal, a synonym.

clue.text: Many snakes are associated with them

definitions.text: Many snakes are associated with them

parts.words: Many snakes are associated with them
parts.note: in the board game the snakes carry you down while other items carry you up the board

explanation.surface: A remark on what reptiles tend to be found with.
explanation.walkthrough: The board game Snakes and Ladders pairs snakes with climbing frames of rungs.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's board game pairs serpents with climbing steps, so the snakes are associated with them.

annotationWithheld.why: A celebrity's due (4'1,5): cryptic definition, LION'S SHARE (lion = celebrity). Annotation is sound but apply refuses it: keep_spelling auto-adds spelling LION'S SHARE from known_spellings (enumeration regex ignores the apostrophe), then format_problems refuses that spelling as derived from the separators. Tool conflict, not a clue fault.

indicators.note: the word anagram itself says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reference work listing words that signal rearrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagram' rearranges INDICATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference volume of words and meanings is a kind of book.

clue.text: Fresh loans required for a hairdressing business

indicators.note: fresh means renewed, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: New loans are needed for a barber's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges LOANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty parlour or barber's premises is a stylist's establishment.

clue.text: Animal in a role that gives limited protection

indicators.note: in places the animal inside the word for a role

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: An actor in an animal costume plays a part offering only partial cover.
explanation.walkthrough: APE goes inside PART; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall along a roof or bridge edge offers only partial shelter or a barrier against falls.
Both a newspaper printed every day, and a scholarly essay or study.

parts.note: the proverb says the devil finds work for idle hands, so he was the original employment agent

explanation.surface: A reference to the earliest employment agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb that the devil finds work for idle hands makes the fiend an employment agent.

clue.text: One hundred in it is twice reduced by 50%

indicators.note: in places the hundred inside the word one

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A puzzle in arithmetic about halving something twice.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside ONE. Twice reduced by fifty per cent: two halved becomes a single time.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times halved gives a single time, so a quantity of twice cut in half is a single occasion.

clue.text: It enables one to pass as a traveller

definitions.text: It enables one to pass as a traveller

parts.words: It enables one to pass as a traveller
parts.note: a stamp in a passport lets a foreign tourist through a border, not a disguise

explanation.surface: Something that helps a person pose convincingly as a tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport endorsement permits entry through a border, letting a voyager pass.

clue.text: Thus three-quarters of the beer is not drunk

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: three-quarters of a four-letter word leaves three letters, losing one

explanation.surface: Leaving most of a pint untouched keeps one clear-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters of' drops one E from BEER, leaving BER after SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Not intoxicated is the plain meaning, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: shipwreck means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: here the possessive S counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe's wreck was the start of his adventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipwreck' rearranges CRUSOES, including the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where something starts are its beginnings, a synonym.
Both narrate a story, and count votes a second time, as in an election.

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheese list has not been issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges LISTNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-veined English variety, an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Take over from a king and two biblical characters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, a king
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Replacing a monarch and a pair of figures from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace someone on duty is to free them, a synonym of taking a shift over.

clue.text: With a look, the little devil may injure one

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite with a certain expression may hurt someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With', 'may' and 'one' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or weaken is to harm, a synonym.

indicators.note: in places one word inside the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a measure of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medal pinned on punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: ON goes inside HOUR; 'put' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal or title awarded is an award of distinction, so a decoration.

indicators.note: held by means the letters sit inside the words Uncle Frank

explanation.surface: A relative named Frank is keeping hold of a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' points to the run inside uncLE Frank.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical symbol fixing pitch on the stave is a key in that sense.

clue.text: House in the Home Counties on the motorway

parts.note: the Home Counties, the counties round London, lie in the South East, SE
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, read as MI

explanation.surface: A house in commuter country near the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house shares one wall, a type of dwelling.
Both computed by arithmetic, and intended with forethought, as in a planned insult.

definitions.meaning: steak cooked only briefly, red inside

explanation.definitionFit: Both scarce or uncommon, and lightly cooked so the steak stays red inside.

clue.text: Fairy tales may give a sort of security, perhaps

indicators.note: may give suggests the letters can be reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Bedtime stories might bring a child comfort and a feeling of safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may give' rearranges FAIRYTALES.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier or handrail protecting from falls is an example of security.
